question: Which state of the matter has LEAST force of attraction between its particles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gases have the least force of attraction between their particles compared to solids, liquids, and plasma.
 
• The particles in a gas are widely spaced and move freely and rapidly in all directions.
 
• This weak force of attraction allows gases to fill any container they are placed in, taking the shape and volume of the container.
 
• Due to minimal intermolecular forces, gases can be compressed easily and have low densities.
 
• The kinetic energy of gas particles is higher than that of solids and liquids, leading to greater movement and lower attraction between particles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solid State**:

 
 
• In solids, particles are closely packed in a fixed, orderly arrangement, resulting in strong intermolecular forces of attraction.
 
• This strong attraction gives solids a definite shape and volume.
 
 
 
• **Liquid State**:
 
 
• Liquids have a moderate level of attraction between particles, allowing them to flow and take the shape of their container while retaining a fixed volume.
 
• The particles in a liquid are less tightly packed than in a solid but are closer together than in a gas.
 
 
 
• **Plasma State**:
 
 
• Plasma consists of highly energized particles with sufficient energy to overcome the attraction between electrons and nuclei, resulting in a collection of free-moving ions and electrons.
 
• It is often referred to as the fourth state of matter and is found in stars, including the sun, and in man-made objects like neon signs and plasma TVs.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Theory of Gases**:
 
 
• This theory explains the behavior of gases based on the idea that gas particles are in constant, random motion and that their collisions with the walls of a container cause pressure.
 
• It also states that the temperature of a gas is proportional to the average kinetic energy of its particles.
